cells.tense: You are with someone right now and the pull between you is live and warm. The whole shape of it sits in your hands. Now you can sort which feelings to hand forward.
cells.act: work the pattern through to its logic
cells.ask: Take the thing that keeps happening with someone you care about and lay it out on paper as a pattern — what starts it, what it does, where it lands. Keep reading your own writing until the next step is obvious.
cells.core:
You are with someone right now and several feelings are offered at once, each one warm and possible. The reach between you is live. You don't have to take them all — sorting which ones are actually true is the work sitting with you, and the true ones land harder for being fewer.

Work the pattern through to its logic this week, on paper: the thing that keeps happening with someone you care about. Write what starts it, what it does between you, where it lands, and read until the next step is plain. You'll lose some of the atmosphere that made the moment pleasant. What you keep is a step that holds, taken toward someone real, by your own hand.

cells.tense: You will be braced for so many versions of the connection that none will be allowed to happen at the pace it wants. You carry the shape of five friendships you have not had yet.
cells.act: protect what was won by the ending
cells.ask: Pick the friendship you keep holding open to every possible version, and note the plain truth of what it is this week — the shape it already has. Then leave that shape alone rather than pumping it for more.
cells.core:
You will be braced for so many versions of the connection that none will be allowed to happen at the pace it wants. The pull to gather people runs faster than the people themselves — five possible friendships already arranged, warmth held open against outcomes, and the others can feel the waiting they're standing in.

Protect what was won by the ending. Pick the friendship you keep holding open to every possible version, and note the plain truth of what it is this week, then leave that shape alone rather than pumping it for more. Keeping it at that size is not loss; it's holding what you already have. The live part of the friendship gets its own pace back.

cells.tense: What you felt with someone stayed at a door you have already walked past. You were part of it, and then you stood outside it.
cells.act: put the problem down and take a walk with nothing to solve
cells.ask: When the pull to reach someone runs strong this week, put the problem down and take a walk with nothing to solve. No reaching, no fixing the warmth — just the walk, the pull left where it is.
cells.core:
What you felt with someone stayed at a door you have already walked past. The warmth was there, you were part of it, and then the moment closed behind you with the reach still unspent, still looking backward for what it missed. When the pull is working well, it moves you toward someone and lands. Lately it circles instead, rereading what already happened.

So put the problem down and take a walk with nothing to solve. When the pull runs strong this week, go outside and leave it alone — no reaching, no fixing the warmth. Connection isn't a task you finish. The quiet gives your system what it needs to come back to what's here, and what already exists with them is enough to stand in.
cells.sheetLine: The warmth is already here, so stop reaching past it.

cells.tense: You steer people toward the good thing you feel with them and tell yourself you are only following them. The pull that gathers them runs your hand.
cells.act: reason it from first principles once
cells.ask: Pick the connection you most often tune so it stays warm. Before you adjust it again, reason it from first principles once — the simplest true sentence about the two of you — then leave the next move alone for a day.
cells.core:
You steer people toward the good thing you feel with them and tell yourself you are only following them. The pull that gathers them runs your hand, and the steering hasn't been counted as yours, so it goes on correcting for the warmth you want to find.

Reason it from first principles once. Pick the connection you most often tune so it stays warm, write the simplest true sentence about the two of you, no arranging, then leave the next move alone for a day. That sentence names where your attention already is, and naming it hands you back the wheel. The pull is real and it's yours.
